questions.stem: A substance has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container. What state of matter is it in?

options.text: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Plasma

questions.explanation: Liquids have a fixed volume (particles are close together) but no fixed shape (particles can slide past each other), so they take the shape of their container. Solids have both fixed shape and volume. Gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume and expand to fill the entire container.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the arrangement and movement of particles in a gas?

options.text: Particles are in a regular pattern and vibrate in fixed positions
Particles are close together and slide over each other
Particles are far apart and move randomly at high speeds
Particles are far apart but do not move

questions.explanation: Gas particles are widely spaced with no regular arrangement and move randomly at high speeds in all directions. Option A describes a solid. Option B describes a liquid. Particles in all states above absolute zero have kinetic energy and are in motion.

questions.stem: Ice, liquid water, and steam are all made of H2O molecules. Why do they behave differently?

options.text: They contain different types of molecules
The molecules have different amounts of kinetic energy, affecting how they are arranged and move
The molecules are different sizes in each state
The molecules have different masses in each state

questions.explanation: The same H2O molecules behave differently because they have different amounts of kinetic energy at different temperatures. In ice, particles vibrate in fixed positions with low KE. In water, they have enough energy to move past each other. In steam, they have enough energy to overcome all intermolecular forces. The molecules themselves are identical in all three states.

questions.stem: A sealed syringe contains air. When the plunger is pushed in, the volume decreases. Which state of matter allows this compression, and why?

options.text: Gas - because gas particles are far apart with large spaces between them
Liquid - because liquid particles can slide past each other
Solid - because solid particles vibrate and can be pushed closer
Gas - because gas particles are smaller than liquid particles

questions.explanation: Gases are easily compressed because their particles are far apart with large gaps between them. Pushing the plunger forces the particles closer together into a smaller volume. Liquids and solids are very difficult to compress because their particles are already close together. Gas particles are not smaller; the same molecules can exist in any state.

questions.stem: Which property explains why you can smell perfume from across a room?

options.text: Perfume particles are pushed across by air currents only
Gas particles diffuse - they spread from high to low concentration due to random motion
Perfume molecules are attracted to your nose
Perfume changes from liquid to solid in the air

questions.explanation: Perfume molecules evaporate and become gas particles. These move randomly in all directions, spreading from areas of high concentration (near the perfume) to low concentration (across the room). This process is called diffusion. While air currents help, diffusion occurs even in still air due to the random kinetic motion of particles.
